engineering_content.technology_domain: Piezoresistive Sensing + Tubing Mechanics + Drift Compensation

system_architecture.description: Catheter-integrated piezoresistive pressure sensor with self-referencing architecture for drift compensation. R1 fix: original P-27 suffered from chronic drift; R1 redesign adds self-referencing bridge for drift correction.

subsystems.name: Piezoresistive sensing element (MEMS)
subsystems.function: Converts mechanical stress to resistance change via piezoresistive effect

subsystems.name: Self-referencing bridge (R1 fix)
subsystems.function: Compensates for thermal and temporal drift by referencing active sensor to dummy/passive element
subsystems.evidence_source: R1 fix + external drift compensation literature (sciencedirect S0924424724006095)

subsystems.name: Catheter integration (mechanical protection)
subsystems.function: Mounts sensor in catheter wall; protects from mechanical damage while transmitting pressure

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning + telemetry
subsystems.function: Amplifies, filters, digitizes sensor signal; transmits to external reader

key_equations: dR/R = pi_L * sigma_L + pi_T * sigma_T [piezoresistive effect]
sensor_model.sensing_principle: dR/R = pi_L * sigma_L + pi_T * sigma_T (piezoresistive effect in silicon); Wheatstone bridge converts resistance change to voltage
sensor_model.self_referencing_architecture: Active sensor exposed to pressure; dummy sensor shielded from pressure but exposed to same temperature; bridge output cancels thermal drift
sensor_model.critical_parameter: Gauge factor GF, bridge excitation V_ex, drift rate
sensor_model.R1_correction: Original P-27 used single-element sensor with chronic drift; R1 redesign adds dummy element for differential measurement

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: Pressure on catheter deforms MEMS diaphragm; piezoresistive elements on diaphragm change resistance; Wheatstone bridge outputs voltage proportional to pressure
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Piezoresistive effect: dR/R = pi * sigma, where pi is piezoresistive coefficient (typically 10^-11 to 10^-10 Pa^-1 for silicon, much higher than metal strain gauges). Wheatstone bridge: V_out = (dR / (4R + 2*dR)) * V_ex ≈ (dR / (4R)) * V_ex for small dR.

self_referencing_model.model: V_out = (R_active(T,P) - R_dummy(T)) / (4*R) * V_ex; thermal drift in R_dummy cancels with R_active
self_referencing_model.drift_compensation_target: Reduce drift from typical 1-10 mmHg/month to < 0.5 mmHg/month (MODEL_DERIVED target)
self_referencing_model.status: MODELLED — no hardware validation of drift performance

governing_model.summary: Piezoresistive pressure sensing with Wheatstone bridge and self-referencing drift compensation. Bridge output proportional to pressure-induced resistance change; dummy element cancels thermal drift.
equations: dR/R = pi_L * sigma_L + pi_T * sigma_T [piezoresistive effect]
P_measured = V_out / (S * V_ex) [pressure from voltage, S = sensitivity]
assumptions: Piezoresistive coefficients stable over implantation lifetime (UNKNOWN for chronic)
Bridge elements matched to within tolerance
Self-referencing architecture cancels thermal drift (UNKNOWN — depends on matching)

boundary_conditions: Sensor size: constrained by catheter geometry
parameter_sensitivities: pi (piezoresistive coefficient) — varies with doping and crystal orientation; typical Si pi ~ 10^-11 to 10^-10 Pa^-1
V_ex (excitation voltage) — linear scaling of output; higher V_ex = better SNR but more power
R (bridge element resistance) — affects power consumption and noise
Matching between R_active and R_dummy — affects drift cancellation quality

Bridge element mismatch — thermal drift not cancelled
Packaging failure — CSF ingress damages electronics
Catheter kink damages sensor — mechanical failure

engineering_core.external_precedent: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT ≠ INVENTION_VALIDATION — published chronically implanted pressure sensor literature (PMC4279503) establishes that piezoresistive sensors can be implanted and that drift is a major challenge. Published drift compensation literature (sciencedirect S0924424724006095) establishes that self-referencing architectures can compensate thermal drift. They do NOT establish that the proposed catheter-integrated sensor achieves target drift performance in CSF.
